e4409f918115: 1. The three components: when to use each
3c1479d477e9: MultiDatePick ships three Lightning Web Components on one shared base. Pick the one that matches your data.
f27f7b687328: Pick many dates at once. Best for RSVPs, attendance, time off, blackout dates and holiday calendars.
7f57434a10df: In the builders: MultiDatePick - Dates & Times
40a199d4fa7f: Dates plus time slots. Best for classes, appointments, training blocks and shifts.
425a71b74350: In the builders: MultiDatePick - Resource Booking
fc87e97323ab: Dates, times and a resource. Best for rooms, equipment, people and anything with capacity.
0c1b0e08e992: Features stack. Everything on Date is also on Date Time and Booking. Date Time adds times. Booking adds resources and capacity.
9a0315a5fe3b: 2. Record shapes: when to use each
558c91a41424: A record shape is how a selection turns into records. It comes from three independent choices, and every combination works.
bb210301ab8c: <t1>Date Time / Booking</t1>: each record has a start and end time.
292a43acf087: <t1>Add-on:</t1> turn on <t2>Consolidate Time Span</t2> for one parent record across the whole time range, plus a sub-block child for each gap inside it.
6c6db756b66f: <t1>None</t1>: Date, Date Time, or Booking without a resource.
fb1c3064c729: <t1>Single resource</t1>: Booking with a resource dropdown.
46f63fa20f7a: <t1>Multiple resources</t1>: Booking with checkboxes, one record per checked resource.
c767833aba93: <t1>Per click</t1>: each selected date is its own record. Five clicks, five records.
f7722993332b: <t1>Per range</t1>: back-to-back dates become one record with a start and end. Set <t2>End Date Field API Name</t2>.
2171395342b6: The Setup Wizard names six shapes: <t1>one record per date</t1>, <t2>one per date range</t2>, <t3>one per time block</t3>, <t4>parent plus sub-blocks</t4>, <t5>single resource</t5> and <t6>multiple resources</t6>.
8e52743ee8d9: Answer three questions per scenario to land on a shape. The Setup Wizard asks the same three.

5f68489bcf7f: <t1>Do you need a resource picker?</t1> No.

f3dbbb3c8217: → <t1>Per range</t1>: one record, start Mon, end Fri.

6c1d098a9558: <t1>Do you need times?</t1> Yes, the same start and end each day.
48ed09db6592: <t1>Do you need a resource picker?</t1> Yes, several rooms with checkboxes.

ab059598dc22: <t1>One record per date</t1><x2/>1 date → 1 record.<x3/><t4>Use for:</t4> RSVPs, attendance, daily check-ins.
314ca71ece5a: <t1>One record per date range</t1><x2/>Back-to-back dates → 1 record with start and end.<x3/><t4>Use for:</t4> PTO, travel, multi-night stays.

4275af1f2f1d: <t1>One record per time block</t1><x2/>1 date × 1 time block = 1 record.<x3/><t4>Use for:</t4> timesheets, shift segments, training blocks.
d3f8524f3273: Range with a shared time block. Back-to-back dates with the same times → 1 record.<x1/><t2>Use for:</t2> multi-day training with the same hours each day.
2d48bd06281c: <t1>Date Time + Consolidate Time Span</t1><x2/><t3>Parent record plus sub-block children for gaps</t3>
bc2781fbfdd7: <t1>Parent plus sub-blocks</t1><x2/>One parent spans the full time range. Each gap inside it becomes a sub-block child.<x3/><t4>Use for:</t4> training with lunch breaks, field routes with travel between stops.

1621eef8ded3: <t1>Single resource</t1><x2/>1 record per date × time block, tied to the resource.<x3/><t4>Use for:</t4> conference rooms, trainer scheduling.
f1473878047c: Single resource range. Back-to-back dates on one resource → 1 record per range.<x1/><t2>Use for:</t2> multi-night room stays, multi-day equipment checkout.
a7cd525d430d: <t1>Multiple resources</t1><x2/>1 record per resource × date × time block.<x3/><t4>Use for:</t4> parallel team meetings, multi-room training.
1c00626448a6: Multiple resource range. Back-to-back dates across N resources → N records, one per resource.<x1/><t2>Use for:</t2> a week of training in 3 rooms at once.
ac6fb29bc1a7: <t1>Booking + Consolidate Time Span</t1><x2/><t3>Parent booking plus sub-block gap children</t3>
bd35088da988: Booking parent plus sub-blocks. A resource booked all day with its breaks on record.<x1/><t2>Use for:</t2> lab equipment with maintenance windows.
d53b0d0b9c4b: <t1>Bottom line:</t1> any combination of the three choices works. If your scenario is not a named pattern, set each choice on its own and the component does the rest.

b5ed67953bd0: The two sound alike but do opposite things. <t1>Blocking</t1> takes availability away: the slot shows but cannot be booked. <t2>Hiding</t2> takes records out of view, which frees their slots.

a81cc8a12a5c: No booking exists; you are marking it off-limits

c9e12827b156: API name of a Number field on the resource object defining the maximum concurrent bookings per time slot. When set, slots display an X/Y badge and stay available until full. Ideal for training rooms, hot desks, or class registrations. Leave blank for one-booking-per-slot behavior. Example: Capacity__c
5542eda127bd: CAPACITY BOOKING MODE ONLY (requires Capacity Field). Controls how X/Y capacity is calculated when multiple resources are selected. COMBINED (default) sums bookings AND capacities: best when each resource is independent inventory (e.g. 4 records across 4 rooms with capacity 5 each = 4/20). DISTINCT counts unique events (records sharing the same date + start time + end time across resources count as ONE) and uses the MAX single-resource capacity: best when one event spans multiple resources simultaneously (4 records across 4 rooms = 1/5).
3dc97fcfeb56: When ON, shows availability details in the resource panel (e.g. '3/5 days available'). Helps users choose the best resource before booking. Requires Resource Object API Name to be configured.
fe549c5f0184: Controls what happens when selected dates have time conflicts with existing records. 'block' (default): save is blocked and conflicting dates are highlighted. 'skip': save proceeds but conflicting dates are skipped. 'allow': no conflict checking. Only applies in grid-shared mode (Time Display Mode='grid' + Allow Different Times Per Date=OFF).
db15ac439b91: Minutes kept free after every existing booking for cleanup or turnaround, per resource on Booking. A time that would start inside the buffer counts as taken everywhere availability is shown (time grid, capacity counts, Week drag) and at Save, and Conflict Behavior decides what happens. Example: 15 leaves a quarter hour between meetings in the same room.
36d9c3622f68: Number of days ahead to check for time slot conflicts and load availability. Default: 360. Reduce for better performance on high-volume objects.
7a45acb40de2: When ON, selected time slots output as a single span from first slot start to last slot end. Gaps between selected slots auto-turn orange and are tracked as sub-blocks. Use for scheduling scenarios where you need a full shift span (e.g. 9 AM-5 PM) while separately tracking breaks. Only applies in grid mode.
d8f0ac030848: When set, adds a toggle button letting users manually mark slots as sub-blocks (orange). Useful for sub-blocks at the edge of the work span. Leave blank to use auto-orange only. Example: 'Mark as Break', 'Mark as Lunch'. Requires Consolidate Time Span to be ON.
744d85889e84: When ON, displays the sub-block toggle button in the time grid header. Requires Consolidate Time Span to be ON and Sub-Block Button Label to be set.
f3df2d4e429e: API name of the child object for sub-block records. Example: Work_Break__c. Requires Consolidate Time Span to be ON and Click to Save mode (Parent Record Id set).
98350c867ef8: Lookup field on the sub-block object linking to the parent record. Example: Shift__c. Required when Sub-Block Object is set.
545862ca88dd: Date field on the sub-block object. Example: Break_Date__c. Required when Sub-Block Object is set.
52a40730f5e8: Start Time field on the sub-block object. Example: Break_Start__c. Required when Sub-Block Object is set.
e70c0b1bb32a: End Time field on the sub-block object. Example: Break_End__c. Required when Sub-Block Object is set.
304799c3efbd: Text field on the sub-block object to store a label. Example: Break_Name__c. Required when Sub-Block Object is set.
c97ec4bb68f9: API name of an object to query for dates that should be blocked from selection. Example: Public_Holiday__c
2358ab5586bc: API name of the Date field on the blocked dates object. Requires Blocked Dates Object to be set.
19d6297cb963: Optional: Time field on the blocked object marking the START of a partial-day closure. When both Start and End Time fields are set and a blocked record carries both, only that time range is closed on the date (the rest stays bookable). Leave blank for whole-day blocking.
1cf6ed27f7ba: Optional: Time field on the blocked object marking the END of a partial-day closure. Pairs with Blocked Dates Start Time Field.
7052c778f989: Optional: narrows an existing closure to one resource. Give the API name of a lookup/resource field on the blocked object; when a blocked record's resource matches the calendar's selected resource, only that resource is closed for the time range. Leave it blank and each closure applies to ALL resources (region-wide). Blocking itself is switched on by Blocked Dates Source Object, not by this field. Only meaningful with resource booking.
2cace23978af: Optional: filter field on the blocked object. Two modes: (a) value mode: when Blocked Dates Filter Value is set, scopes blocked records by <field> = <value> (e.g. Status__c = Cancelled). (b) parent-scope mode: when Filter Value is blank, treats this field as a lookup to the current record and scopes by <field> = recordId. Leave blank to block globally.
feb0de1c30ec: Optional: value to filter Blocked Dates Filter Field by. When set, blocked records must match <filterField> = <filterValue> (e.g. Status__c = Cancelled). Lets multiple categories of blockers coexist in the same table: each consumer calendar picks which category applies.
4038b6028796: When ON, populates the Date Ranges JSON output with consecutive dates grouped into ranges. Required if you want to use the MultiDatePickParser action to loop through ranges.
e465f07f493d: OUTPUT: Array of all selected dates in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD). Use this in your Flow to create records or pass to the next screen.
6e88f5ef167a: OUTPUT: JSON of consecutive dates grouped into ranges. Only populated when 'Output Date Ranges as JSON' is ON. Pass to MultiDatePickParser to loop in Flow.
993d874aa1ba: OUTPUT: JSON string with each date and its selected time. Pass to MultiDatePickParser to loop through in your Flow.
206a364cdcea: OUTPUT: JSON of sub-block (gap/break) windows per date. Only populated when Consolidate Time Span is ON. Use in a Flow loop to create child records.
db314e0df497: OUTPUT: Number of booking records successfully created. Use in your Flow to show a confirmation message.
995840ff5fa8: OUTPUT: List of dates where bookings could not be created due to conflicts with existing reservations.
